notes: Right to rest: may decline hours <11 h after the previous shift; 1.5x for each such hour worked.

Predictability pay (FAQ Q12-14): with <14 days but >=24 h notice, 1 h for any change; with <24 h notice, 1 h for adding a shift, adding hours or moving a shift, and min(4, hours cut) for cuts/cancellations (15 min cut = 0.25 h). Paid at the regular rate (29 U.S.C. 207(e)). Grace: 10 min before/after a shift (up to 30 min after to finish serving a customer).

Exemptions (FAQ Q15-16): employee-initiated changes only — shift swaps, coverage arrangements between employees, employee requests to leave early or take sick/vacation days. The FAQ lists no exemption for employer-requested hours the employee voluntarily accepts (voluntary_additional_hours_exempt=false).

Coverage (FAQ Q6): employers with 10+ employees in Berkeley primarily in retail (and other listed industries) with 56+ employees globally; restaurants, retail/restaurant franchisees and nonprofits need 100+ globally. Covers employees working 2+ hours/week in Berkeley; ordinance operational Jan. 12, 2024. Extra key min_local_employees.
Offers of additional hours to existing part-time employees must be made and accepted in writing, with 24 h to respond (FAQ Q20).

params.exemption_note: Only employee-initiated changes are exempt: "Employee-initiated changes like shift swaps or coverage arrangements do not require the employer to pay predictability pay." An employer-requested call-in owes 1 hour even if accepted.

rules.summary: Berkeley (10+ local and 56+ global employees in retail): inside 14 days, 1 hour at the regular rate for any change with 24 h+ notice and for added/moved shifts with less; cuts/cancellations with <24 h notice pay the hours cut, up to 4.

citation.excerpt: If the employer cancels an employee's shift or reduces the hours in a shift with less than 24 hours' notice, the employer owes the employee 4 hours of predictability pay or the number of hours reduced

rules.summary: Hours worked less than 11 hours after the previous shift are paid at 1.5x, and the employee may decline them.

citation.excerpt: For every hour worked less than 11 hours after the end of the previous shift, an employee should be paid time and a half.
